shorts.title: What you will learn: Variables and types
shorts.hook: Every value in your program lives in a box with a type.
shorts.script: Every value in your program lives in a box with a type. Until now, our programs only printed words. Today they learn to remember things. You will make boxes for numbers, letters and yes or no answers. A variable is a named box in memory. Every box has a type, and the type says what can go inside. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Variables and types.

shorts.title: Variables and types in one minute
shorts.hook: A variable is a named box in memory.
shorts.script: A variable is a named box in memory. Every box has a type, and the type says what can go inside. Int holds whole numbers, like three fish. Double holds numbers with a decimal point. Char holds one single character. Bool holds only true or false. Think of a beach shack fridge. One shelf is for bottles, and one tray is for ice. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Variables and types in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: The sizeof operator tells us how many bytes a type needs.
shorts.script: The sizeof operator tells us how many bytes a type needs. For int, it prints four. A double needs eight bytes. A char needs one byte. A bool needs one byte as well. These numbers match the boxes we saw before. Each line shows the size of one type. The numbers are four, eight, one and one. A variable is a named box with a type. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A variable with no starting value
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in variables and types?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in variables and types? Bug of the Day. Here we make an int called packets, but we never give it a value. The compiler warns us that packets is used uninitialized. The program still builds, but it prints a strange number. That number is garbage left in memory. Give every variable a value when you make it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: A variable with no starting value.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you make four variables and print them in variables and types?
shorts.script: Can you make four variables and print them in variables and types? An uninitialised variable walks into a bar. The bartender asks, what will you have? It says, whatever was there before. Make four variables: your age, your height in metres, your first initial and whether you like fish. Print all four. Write your answer in the comments. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
